candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Epistle of Enoch (1 Enoch 91-108) (c. 100 BC)

'And when sin and unrighteousness and blasphemy and violence in all kinds of deeds increase, and apostasy and transgression and uncleanness increase, a great chastisement shall come from heaven upon all these' — the Epistle's doctrine of escalating sin meeting decisive divine judgment. The catalog of sins (sin / unrighteousness / blasphemy / violence / apostasy / transgression / uncleanness) is exhaustive in its mapping of moral disorder. The 'great chastisement from heaven' Tewahedo reads as both proximate (the historical judgments that fall on civilizations) and ultimate (the final eschatological judgment). The verse anchors the Tewahedo tradition's correlation between societal-moral decline and divine response — a hermeneutic regularly applied in monastic-prophetic preaching.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Apocalypse of Weeks (1 Enoch 93)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Apocalypse of Weeks (1 Enoch 93) (c. 150 BC)

'And after that there shall be another, the eighth week, that of righteousness, and a sword shall be given to it that a righteous judgement may be executed on the oppressors, and sinners shall be delivered into the hands of the righteous. And at its close they shall acquire houses through their righteousness, and a house shall be built for the Great King in glory for evermore' — eighth week: messianic age, the righteous receive the sword to execute judgment. Tewahedo ecclesiology preserves the 'house built for the Great King for ever' as the Tewahedo qǝddǝst's eschatological function: the Tewahedo tabot-house is provisionally that house already.

candidates.draft_body:

'And after that, in the ninth week, the righteous judgement shall be revealed to the whole world, and all the works of the godless shall vanish from all the earth, and the world shall be written down for destruction' — ninth week: cosmic revelation of judgment. The verbal parallel to Rev 20:11-15 (the books opened, the world judged) is preserved in Tewahedo eschatological readings as Enochic anticipation of the Johannine vision.

candidates.source_name: 1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) / Apocalypse of Weeks (1 Enoch 93)
candidates.draft_body:
1 Enoch (Ethiopian tradition) Apocalypse of Weeks (1 Enoch 93) (c. 150 BC)

'And after this, in the tenth week in the seventh part, there shall be the great eternal judgement, in which He will execute vengeance amongst the angels' — tenth week: final judgment of the fallen Watchers. This closes the Watchers arc that began in 1En 6 and was preliminarily judged at 1En 10 / 88:1 / 90:24: the Apocalypse of Weeks holds out the final judgment-of-angels until the LAST week of cosmic time. Tewahedo demonology preserves the two-stage temporal pattern: bound now, judged finally then.

candidates.draft_body:

'And the first heaven shall depart and pass away, and a new heaven shall appear, and all the powers of the heavens shall give sevenfold light' — new heaven appears with sevenfold light. The Apocalypse of Weeks' eschatological climax is verbally parallel to Rev 21:1 ('a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away') with the Enochic distinctive emphasis on SEVENFOLD-light (parallel to Isa 30:26 'the light of the sun shall be sevenfold').
